title: TCP vs UDP: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: There are two ways to send data across a network. One is like certified mail. The other is like a postcard. Which one you need depends on the job.

scenes.heading: Certified mail or postcard
scenes.narration: Certified mail is T C P. You fill in a form, pay for tracking, and get a signature back as proof. If it gets lost, you find out and send it again. It's reliable, but all that paperwork takes time. A postcard is U D P. You scribble a message, drop it in the box, and hope for the best. There's no receipt and no resend, but it's very quick. That's why video calls use postcards, and file downloads use certified mail.

scenes.heading: Side by side
scenes.narration: Here's the comparison. T C P sets up a connection first, using a handshake. U D P just sends. T C P has a bigger header, between twenty and sixty bytes. U D P's header is always exactly eight. And for apps, web and email use T C P, while D N S queries, voice and streaming use U D P.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. U D P isn't faster because its packets are smaller. It's faster because it skips setup, receipts and resends. T C P can't promise delivery on a broken link. It only tells you when it gave up. And U D P still has port numbers, just like T C P.

items.wrong: UDP is faster because packets are smaller
items.right: It skips setup, acknowledgments and resends
On a dead link it gives up and reports failure
It has source and destination ports

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva TCP and UDP lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. T C P is reliable but slower, and U D P is fast but has no guarantees. The exam trick is to match the app. Files use T C P, and streaming uses U D P. D N S queries use U D P, but zone transfers use T C P. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva TCP and UDP lab.

points.t: TCP: reliable. UDP: fast, no guarantees
Match the app: files = TCP, streaming = UDP
DNS: UDP for queries, TCP for zone transfers
